sup-45e9b39ec46a9e4c-q1:whole.hint: Work out the direction of each electric-field contribution using a positive test charge.
notes: For a point charge, |E| = k|Q|/r² and force is F = qE. Add fields as vectors; a negative test charge experiences force opposite the field.
Unlike charges attract and like charges repel. Keep source charge, test charge and their separation distinct when using Coulomb’s law.

sup-45e9b39ec46a9e4c-q2:whole.hint: The conductor can redistribute its charges even if its net charge stays zero.
notes: A nearby charge polarizes a neutral conductor: opposite charge is attracted towards the nearer side and like charge moves farther away.
Because electric forces depend on distance, equal amounts of separated positive and negative charge need not produce cancelling forces on the nearby charge.

notes: Electric field lines point from positive towards negative charges, and their tangent gives the local field direction. Closer lines represent a stronger field.
